A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of repetitive perivascular stimulation on glucose output and lactate metabolism are not mediated via norepinephrinergic nerves.
the metabolic and hemodynamic responses of the perfused liver during repetitive nerve stimulation are not mediated by norepinephrinergic mechanisms.
the metabolic and hemodynamic responses to repetitive stimulation of perivascular nerves in the perfused liver were not related to the release of norepinehrine.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of repetitive stimulation on glucose output, lactate and portal flow are mediated by other mechanisms than norepinephine overflow.
norepinephrinergic nerve fibers around the portal vein are able to release norepinephine and to increase hepatic glycogenolysis.
the effects of nerve stimulation in perfused liver are not mediated by norepinephrin, and the effects of nerve stimulations are not mediated by a release of catecholamines.
